editorial.headline: Retailing Soft Furnishings and Surface Finishes in Indonesia
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the retail sale of carpets, curtains, and selected wall and floor coverings—nationally open to foreign ownership, but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is for retailers of the surfaces that give an interior its finish: carpets and rugs, curtains and drapes, and wall and floor coverings including wallpaper, tiles, laminate, and vinyl flooring. Its boundary matters. The scope expressly excludes the retail sale of floor tiles as building materials, keeping this activity focused on the furnishing and finishing side of the retail trade.

It is available across the full business-scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In practical terms, the registered activity should reflect a business genuinely engaged in selling these specified interior products at retail, rather than a broader construction-materials operation. The scope is detailed enough to cover a coherent shop or retail business spanning soft floor coverings, window treatments, and selected decorative or finishing surfaces.

Nationally, the position is clear. The activity is TERBUKA to PMA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. That national openness should not be mistaken for an automatic route into Bali, however. For PMA registration in Bali today, the activity is blocked. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk classification is Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every stated scope, bringing it within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities.

The distinction is consequential rather than technical. A foreign investor may see a nationally open activity with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling, yet still be unable to register it as PMA in Bali under the current provincial position. The Bali restriction is not a reduction of the national ownership percentage; it is a registration block arising from the activity’s risk classification and the Bali moratorium announced in May 2026.
editorial.pullQuote: A nationally open activity with 100% foreign ownership can still be unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
